title: The Home agent, the intern and the campaign agent as policies on one runtime
request: Rebuild the three agents as policies on the shared runtime, one at a time, with the existing tests as the safety net. Keep the Home agent's scripted fallback, its one-turn-per-draft lock and streamed replies; keep the intern's standard plan; put the campaign agent behind the same runtime and gateway, or keep it as an adapter that reports its requests. Delete a loop only when its tests pass on the runtime.
spec: The Home agent, the intern and the campaign agent run on the runtime with their behaviour unchanged. Done when make product-e2e and the agent tests pass, draft/chat.py's and intern/loop.py's own loops are gone, and the campaign agent runs one campaign on the same runtime.
plan: Plan the three moves: the intern on run() with its write_plan and finish as registered tools in a 'session' scope; the Home agent on run() with a model adapter that keeps its streaming and live bubble; the campaign agent stays on LangGraph and NOOA (its specialists return typed answers, not tool calls) with its experiment write going through the registry and a guard and each phase traced.
Draft the runtime and intern changes in the scratchpad while A2.3's gate ran; apply them after A2.3 was committed.
Save a checkpoint when the owner had to restart to free disk; after the restart, find that the four intern test errors were not the full disk but registry tests that knew only the two old scopes.
Move the intern, then the Home agent (with a trace replay test), then the campaign's experiment (run_experiment in a 'campaign' scope behind the campaign guard, with the same refusals and messages).
Make the campaign tests load again in .venv-agent (the test file imported the server, which needs pandas) and add them to make check-all.
Run check-all and the review; fix five regressions with tests; get a re-check; apply its last small fix; commit.

Find why the disk filled: the test suite never removed its temporary folders; give each test command its own TMPDIR removed at the end (separate commit) and, with the owner's yes, delete the old folders.

decisions.decision: The campaign agent stays a LangGraph loop; only its one write, the experiment, becomes a registered tool behind a guard.
decisions.why: Its specialists answer in typed objects, not tool calls, so run() has nothing to drive; its requests already go through the gateway adapter, and the guard keeps the same refusals.

decisions.decision: Only a call that actually ran ends the run or the turn; a refused finish or question goes back to the model.
decisions.why: A refused terminal call that ends the run silently loses the model's report or leaves the person with no message.

decisions.decision: A terminal tool is never refused for the step budget, even when earlier calls in the same reply used it up.
decisions.why: Refusing the report that ends the session throws away the work the budget paid for.

decisions.decision: The draft schemas stop requiring what the handlers default (ask_user needs only the question, set_pack only the key, request_data nothing).
decisions.why: Model calls are now checked against the full schemas; requiring defaulted keys refused small models' reasonable calls.

change: The Home agent and the intern run on agents.run(); their own loops are gone. The runtime gained stop_when, max_replies (Home: 5 requests per message), per-scope contexts, a result size per policy, terminal tools never refused for the budget, and 'only a call that ran ends the run'. write_plan and finish are session-scope tools; Home's steps are traced under the draft's id and returned by GET /api/drafts/{id}. run_experiment is a campaign-scope tool in agentic/campaign_tools.py behind the campaign guard; each campaign phase and experiment is a trace row. Trace files share one lock per path in a process. make check-all runs the campaign tests in .venv-agent.

findings.defect: finish was refused once an earlier call in the same reply had used up the step budget.
findings.scenario: max_steps 3 and one reply [list_samples x4, finish{'report': 'my report'}]: before, the session completed with 'my report'; now it ended budget_exhausted with 'Stopped: the budget of 3 tool calls is used up', and the report was lost.
findings.cause: After the first refused call the run's end reason was 'steps', and the terminal-tool exemption was never evaluated again.
findings.fix: The exemption is evaluated for a terminal tool even when the end reason is already 'steps'.
findings.test: A runtime test with a report after the budget is used in the same reply.
findings.impact: A model that spent its budget and then reported in the same reply lost its report: the session ended 'budget exhausted' and the person saw a stop message instead of the work's result.

findings.defect: A refused write_plan crashed the session.
findings.scenario: First reply write_plan {} or write_plan with a list: the session ended failed with "'NoneType' object is not subscriptable"; before, it completed.
findings.cause: The step summary sliced session['plan'], which starts as None.
findings.fix: The summary uses an empty string when there is no plan.
findings.test: An intern test with a refused write_plan.
findings.impact: A model's first malformed write_plan, a common small-model mistake, ended the whole session as failed with a Python error instead of letting the model correct itself.

findings.defect: A refused finish ended the session as completed with no final text.
findings.scenario: finish {} or finish with report null: the session was completed with final None; before, it ended with the progress note.
findings.cause: The runtime marked the run terminal even though the handler never ran.
findings.fix: Only a terminal call that ran ends the run; a refused one goes back to the model as an error.
findings.test: An intern test where a refused finish is followed by the model's corrected answer.
findings.impact: A malformed finish ended the session as completed with no text at all, so the person got an empty report for a session that looked successful.
alternatives: Keep the run terminal and fill the final text with the progress note, the reviewer's first option: set aside because ending on a refused finish still throws away the model's report; the run now ends only on a terminal call that ran.

findings.defect: A refused ask_user silently ended the Home turn.
findings.scenario: Reply ask_user {'question': 'When is the prediction made?', 'field': 'prediction_time'} (a field outside the enum) or with an extra key: before, the question was posted; now one request, no agent message, and the conversation stalled until the user typed again.
findings.cause: ask_user was in stop_after whether or not it succeeded, and the 'model only talks' fallback did not run because a step existed.
findings.fix: The turn stops on ask_user only when it succeeded (stop_when), or when a simulation started.
findings.test: A draft-flow test with a refused question followed by a second request.
findings.impact: A question with a field outside the enum ended the Home turn with no message at all, so the person waited for an agent that had stopped until they typed again.

findings.defect: The gateway got no verdict for a propose_workflow the schema refused.
findings.scenario: propose_workflow {'title': 'x'}: before, the verdict (False, 'no steps') was reported; now nothing, so A1.3's model-health check undercounted Home failures.
findings.cause: on_step skipped propose_workflow because proposals report their own verdict, but a schema refusal never reached that code.
findings.fix: on_step reports a failed verdict when a propose_workflow call was refused.
findings.test: A draft-flow test reading the verdicts.
findings.impact: Home's schema-refused proposals went unreported to the gateway, so A1.3's model-health check would show the Home model as healthier than it was.

findings.defect: A refused finish counted against the runtime's budget but not against the session's step count.
findings.scenario: Every reply is finish {} under max_steps 3: the session ends 'budget of 3 tool calls is used up' while used.steps shows 0, so a follow-up starts with the whole budget again (still bounded per run).
findings.cause: The session counted every tool except finish.
findings.fix: A finish counts when it was refused.
findings.test: Intern and runtime tests after the re-check.
findings.impact: A session ended by refused finish calls showed 0 steps used, so a follow-up started with the whole budget again; each run stayed bounded, but the session's total did not.

findings.defect: The campaign tests had stopped loading in their own environment.
findings.scenario: In .venv-agent the campaign test file imported the server, which needs pandas, so collection failed and the campaign was not tested at all.
findings.cause: One import at the top of the test file.
findings.fix: The file loads without the server; the one test that needs it skips there; make check-all runs the campaign tests in .venv-agent.
findings.impact: The campaign agent, the one this package changed through an adapter, had no test running at all, so a regression in its experiment guard would have passed every gate.

findings.defect: The test suite filled the disk.
findings.scenario: About 13,600 tmp folders (around 7.8 GB) from one day of test runs were left in the temp directory; the owner had to restart to free space mid-package.
findings.cause: Tests create folders with tempfile.mkdtemp and never remove them.
findings.fix: Each test command gets its own TMPDIR, removed when it ends whatever its result; the old folders were deleted after the owner said yes.
findings.test: A full gate run leaves nothing behind.
findings.impact: The machine ran out of disk mid-package and the owner had to restart; a full disk also makes gates fail for reasons unrelated to the code (it happened again in A4.3).
findings.open: Direct test runs outside make do not get the per-command temporary folder and its cleanup.

outcome: Done: the Home agent and the intern run on agents.run() and their own loops are gone; the campaign's experiment runs through the registry guard and every phase is traced. One deliberate behaviour change: the intern's tool calls are now checked strictly (set_settings max_rows=500000 is refused, not clamped). The gate passed with 454 tests on files and on PostgreSQL, the 8 campaign tests and the four flows; five regressions fixed and re-checked.
lessons: When a refactor makes a check stricter, every 'stop after this tool' rule must ask whether the tool actually ran.
A re-check after fixes finds the edge cases of the fixes (here a refused finish counted in one budget and not the other).
Tests that never clean up their temporary folders will eventually stop the work; give every test command its own temp folder.
risks: Terminal and stop-after rules firing for tools that were refused, now that every call is checked strictly.
The step budget refusing the very report that ends a session, losing the work the budget paid for.
The Home agent's streaming, scripted fallback and one-turn lock regressing when its own loop is removed.
Forcing the campaign agent onto run() although its specialists return typed objects, not tool calls.
Agent tests silently not loading in the agent environment, leaving an agent untested.
